chunks: ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about women: how should they greet when they enter upon a group of people? He said:
The woman says, “ʿAlaykumu al-salām,” and the man says, “Al-salāmu ʿalaykum.”

key_terms.السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ: peace be upon you, as phrased here by a man
key_terms.عَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ: peace be upon you, as phrased here by a woman

ai.seo_question: How should a woman and a man say salām when entering upon a group according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the proper wording of greeting for women and men when entering upon a group. It reflects etiquette and legal guidance concerning social interaction and the prescribed form of salām.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4637 - Ammar Al-Sabati asked Abu Abdullah (as) about how women should greet when they enter upon a group of people.
Imam (as) replied:
"A woman should say, 'Peace be upon you (ʿAlaykum al-Salam),' and a man should say, 'Peace be upon you all (Al-Salam ʿAlaykum).'"
